summary.text: Andy Raven is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election. He has lived in and around Buninyong all his life and has been involved in organising Free Palestine Ballarat and Say No to Racism rallies. His campaign centres on housing security, wages and rents.

prior_roles.role: Rally organiser (Free Palestine Ballarat, Say No to Racism)

priorities.text: people deserve secure housing and a living wage
Every job should have a liveable wage.
Shifting power back to working-class people
Curbing rent rises that burden tenants and force local shops to close

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Belinda Zivkovic is standing as an independent for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The ABC's guide lists this candidate without a biography or website, and we found nothing else published about them as at 9 Nov 2026.

sources.title: Candidates for Eureka District, Victorian Electoral Commission

summary.text: Emma Muir is the Liberal candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election. She and her husband farm at Myrniong, and she is the founder of the Moorabool and Central Highlands Power Alliance, a community group opposed to the Western Renewables Link transmission project. The party says she has a background in small business, communications and advocacy, and that she was Moorabool's Citizen of the Year in 2024.

prior_roles.organisation: Moorabool and Central Highlands Power Alliance

priorities.text: A say for local communities on major infrastructure decisions

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Emma Muir, Liberal for Eureka, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Ian Maxwell Harkness is the Family First candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election. Raised in Victoria and now settled in Ballarat, he has a long list of practical jobs behind him, from motor mechanics, building and farm work to spray painting and caring for people with severe disabilities. He ran for Family First in Wendouree at the 2022 state election and in Ballarat at the 2025 federal election.

occupation.text: Trades, farm and customer service work; disability carer

prior_roles.role: Carer for people with severe disabilities
Volunteer in remote Australia and Papua New Guinea

priorities.text: Stronger families and support for people who are vulnerable

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Ian Harkness, Family First Party Australia

summary.text: Michaela Settle won Buninyong for Labor in 2018 and has held Eureka, the redrawn and renamed seat, since 2022. She ran her family's sheep farm near Ararat and later worked at Ballarat Community Health, and became a minister in April 2026; she is now Minister for Agriculture, Water, and Rural and Regional Development. She is recontesting Eureka in 2026.

occupation.text: Sheep farmer; later marketing manager at Ballarat Community Health

prior_roles.role: Minister for Water; Rural and Regional Development
Parliamentary Secretary for Regional Victoria; Community Sport
Parliamentary Secretary for Regional Development; Agriculture
Government Whip in the Legislative Assembly
Secretary of the parliamentary Labor Party

previous_candidacies.note: Eureka replaced Buninyong at this election.

priorities.text: Regional towns getting the facilities and services capital cities have
Infrastructure, schools, health, roads and jobs for the area
More mental health services close to home

summary.text: Paul Ballinger is the One Nation candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election. Born and raised in Ballarat, he is a director of a mortgage broking business in the city, after earlier work in construction as a carpenter, joiner and site supervisor. He has also run small businesses, among them a video hire shop and a newsagency.

prior_roles.role: Owner of small businesses, including a video hire shop and a newsagency

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Sam McColl is the Greens candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election. Raised in Ararat and now based in Ballarat, he works as a Triple Zero communications officer, rents his home, and is a St John volunteer who serves as a regional manager as well as a first responder. The Greens also ran him in Eureka at the 2022 state election and in Mallee at the 2022 federal election.

prior_roles.role: Volunteer first responder and regional manager
Worker in local not-for-profit arts organisations

priorities.text: Housing, health and climate justice in regional Victoria
Easing living costs and housing pressure and improving access to services in Eureka
A local member who consults people and involves them in decisions

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Wendy Morrison is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Eureka at the 2026 Victorian election, her third state campaign for the party after Buninyong in 2018 and Eureka in 2022. Schooled in Ballarat, she has worked in retail, as a cook and tour host on coach tours around Australia, and in hospitality and office jobs, and is a qualified yoga teacher. Her party page says she has been a member for about 13 years.

occupation.text: Retail, hospitality and office administration work; qualified yoga teacher

priorities.text: Ending the breeding of animals for farming, experiments, racing and entertainment
A fair transition for workers into sustainable industries
Growing plant-based farming and food production and eco-tourism

sources.title: Eureka: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Wendy Morrison for Eureka, Animal Justice Party Victoria
